title: He Makes $4,100/Month Inspecting Houses (No Experience Needed)
promo_conflict: Lou is preparing and promotes a draw inspector training website and course, which could bias his claims about how accessible and lucrative the inspection business is.

idea.name: Construction loan draw inspections
idea.one_liner: Inspect construction sites for lenders or inspection companies, document progress, and earn a fee per inspection.
idea.customer: Banks and lenders, usually through inspection companies and platforms.
idea.offer: Visit a construction site, check progress against the lender's form, take photos, and submit a report.
idea.revenue_model: Per-inspection fees; Lou usually charges about $60–$75, with rates varying by platform and job.

key_quotes.quote: we'll take pictures, we'll inspect, verify the location that we're at, and make sure that what they've said is done
you accept that inspection. I said, Yes. And then you call the builder or the point of contact.
I show up, I take pictures.
I'm acting as the eyes and ears of the bank.

claims.claim: Lou says his average fee is about $65 per inspection.
claims.quote: I've averaged about $65 for inspection.

claims.claim: The host says Lou made over $2,000 a month last year as a part-time retirement gig.
claims.quote: And last year made over $2,000 a month as a part-time retirement gig.

claims.quote: In fact, I took my daughter, who's a stay-at-home mom with three boys, over the last six weeks, too, which she's been on vacation, she's made about $1,200.

claims.quote: they call us back for each of those five phases, and last phase is to finish for the certificate of occupancy

claims.quote: So if it takes five months or 15 months for them to build that house, I'm gonna be going back there once every month, or every 45 days, or whenever they want a draw

claims.claim: Lou says his daughter earned about $1,200–$1,500 after six weeks, two of which she spent on vacation.
claims.quote: Kinda coaster through, mentored her like I was mentored before, over the last six weeks, two of which she's been on vacation, she's made about $1,200, $1,500.

claims.quote: And this thing is doubled the first year and now it's gonna double again this year.

claims.claim: Lou says inspection companies usually expect a report back within 24–48 hours.
claims.quote: The inspection companies usually want this back within 24 to 48 hours.

claims.quote: Sure, depending on accessibility to the construction site, you could do it in the evenings or during the lunch hour, probably 90% of the time.

claims.quote: we're only gonna do three inspections today and by the time we get back home, we've done six because two or three more popped up.

claims.quote: we have an inspection at this location and it will pay $45.

claims.claim: Lou says a draw inspection takes about 20–30 minutes on site.
claims.quote: I'm 20 to 30 minutes on an inspection site doing an inspection for a draw inspection.

claims.claim: Before getting Starlink, Lou spent about an hour at night completing and uploading reports.
claims.quote: And at night, I'd come on and I'd sit there for an hour and fill all this stuff back out, type it in, upload the photos, submit it.

claims.claim: Lou says payment timing varies, with BUILT paying about monthly and Nationwide about every two weeks.
claims.quote: Bill, I think pays once a month, they log everything up, and they send out a payment. I think at the end of the month, I think nationwide pays every two weeks.

claims.claim: Lou says a typical inspection takes about 25–30 minutes on site.
claims.quote: So I'm spending probably between 25 to 30 minutes that decided, depends on the phase of the construction.

claims.claim: Lou says one early-stage visit involved five or six photos and took less than 10 minutes, likely closer to five.
claims.quote: And so I'm taking five or six pictures of that place, and I was done in less than 10 minutes, probably closer to five.

claims.claim: Lou budgets 30 minutes per job, excluding the travel burden he describes.
claims.quote: I factor in 30 minutes per job for every day.

claims.claim: Lou reports monthly income of about $4,100 and expenses of about $972.
claims.quote: If I average $4,100 in a month in income, I've got about $972 in expenses.

claims.quote: That includes 780 in gas, 30 bucks in software, 35 in insurance, probably 50 bucks for my cell phone, and 75 for the Internet.

claims.claim: Lou says he initially aimed for $12 to $500 a month and now averages $4,100 a month; the initial figure is unclear in the transcript.
claims.quote: I wanted to make $12 to $500 in a month and now I've averaged $4,100 a month every month.

claims.claim: Lou usually works two to three days a week, often one full day and two half days.
claims.quote: I work usually two to three days a week. Usually probably one full day and probably two half days or you know, it just depends on the how I can figure things.

claims.claim: Lou's profitability matrix records 91 working hours in a month.
claims.quote: This says I work 91 hours a month.

claims.claim: Lou says he works about 20 hours a week and has completed as many as 16 inspections in one day.
claims.quote: 20 hours a week though, the most number of inspections I've done in a day. I think I've hit 16 and that's a beautiful day.

claims.claim: Lou has heard of other inspectors handling five or six houses in one neighborhood.
claims.quote: there were times where they'll hit a neighborhood that's got five or six, you know, houses going up

claims.claim: Lou has heard one inspector report doing 50 jobs, but expresses doubt about that figure.
claims.quote: I heard one guy tell me 50 and I've heard others with some other numbers that I gotta wonder, how could you really do all that?

claims.claim: Lou says he may travel about 200–250 miles a day.
claims.quote: because I traveled about 200 miles a day, I would say, probably 250 and 200 miles.

claims.claim: The host suggests a worker could earn another $60–$70 by fitting in a draw inspection between jobs.
claims.quote: if you're a gig economy type of worker, you know, it's on again, off again. And it's like, okay, I could go over here in between jobs and make another 60, 70 bucks.

acquisition_channels.details: Lou signed up with Nationwide Loan Inspectors and gets jobs through platforms or inspection companies including BUILT, RAZE, Landgirl, and Inspection Pros.
A friend introduced Lou to the work, and an inspector mentored him.

ideas.delivery: Lou travels to construction sites, verifies the requested work against a bank or lender checklist, takes location-stamped photos, and submits a report through the ordering company's app or website. The field inspection and travel are done by the inspector.

prices: 780 gas, 30 software, 35 insurance, about 50 phone, 75 internet

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR would apply to homeowner names, addresses, inspection photos, and location data handled in reports; construction-site access and safety rules would also need to be followed.

idea.name: Short-term rental maintenance and checkups
idea.one_liner: Check absentee owners' short-term rentals between guests or monthly, do routine checks and minor tasks, and report the property's condition for a visit fee.
idea.customer: Short-term rental owners who live far from the property.
idea.offer: Check filters, doors, windows, damage, and general condition; take photos, report findings, and help arrange follow-up work.
idea.revenue_model: Lou charges about $150 per visit; the host's $200 monthly subscription suggestion is hypothetical.

I'll go out through the steps of that and take pictures and give a report on everything I see.
